images.filename: Bridge over the River Bann near the Corbet - geograph.org.uk - 171980.jpg
images.caption: Bridge over the River Bann near the Corbet. About 4 miles east of Banbridge the River Bann is crossed by a fine stone bridge at the Drone Hill Road, Tullyconnaught near the Corbet. This is the bridge from road level looking north.  The road connects the Banbridge-Castlewellan road to the Banbridge-Rathfriland road.

images.caption:
Christie Park, Coleraine. 


Christie Park runs from the Bann Bridge to the Sandelford Bridge between the River Bann and the Strand Road.  The Lady Sandel  a 50 foot boat carrying 60 passengers  is expected to operate river cruises from the park starting in July 2006.
images.alt:
Christie Park, Coleraine. 


Christie Park runs from the Bann Bridge to the Sandelford Bridge between the River Bann and the Strand Road.  The Lady Sandel  a 50 foot boat carrying 60 passengers  is expected to operate river cruises from the park starting in July 2006.

images.caption: Coleraine ring road. The Coleraine ring road takes most through traffic away from the town centre.  The section from the Lodge Road to the Strand Road crosses the River Bann by a box-girder bridge called the Sandelford Bridge.  This is the view across the bridge to the Strand Road.
images.alt: Coleraine ring road. The Coleraine ring road takes most through traffic away from the town centre.  The section from the Lodge Road to the Strand Road crosses the River Bann by a box-girder bridge called the Sandelford Bridge.  This is the view across the bridge to the Strand Road.

images.filename: "The Lady Sandel" on the Bann (1) - geograph.org.uk - 220953.jpg
images.caption: "The Lady Sandel" on the Bann (1) The River Bann can be quite attractive as it flows from Lough Neagh to the Atlantic near Castlerock.  A previous attempt, in the mid-90s, to operate cruises on the river failed partly due to the lack of tourists.  Things have changed and The Lady Sandel is now operating successfully from Christie Park at Coleraine.  She is seen heading upstream past the picnic site near Camus.  This trip was fully booked.

images.filename: Anglers at Carnroe, River Bann - geograph.org.uk - 235041.jpg
images.caption: Anglers at Carnroe, River Bann. The Lower Bann at Carnroe is known for its salmon fishery.  Two anglers are seen applying their skills.
images.alt: Anglers at Carnroe, River Bann. The Lower Bann at Carnroe is known for its salmon fishery.  Two anglers are seen applying their skills.

images.caption:
Carnroe lock, River Bann (1) 
The Lower Bann is navigable from Lough Neagh to the Barmouth near Castlerock.  There is a weir at Carnroe near Ballymoney.  The river is by-passed by means of a lock.  This is the view of the lock looking towards Coleraine.
